_description: Structural vectors (spec/VERIFICATION.md V2-3, V2-4, V2-5, V2-6, V2-12). Under verifier_policy at verification_time, base and the positives MUST verify and every case MUST be rejected. Each case names the rule it breaks, the paths it changes from the base, its control (the base, and for the session case also its twin) and the failures that tools/conformance/structural-checks.js computes for it without any SDK. Policy mode: the passport risk_tier medium selects risk_overrides.medium (hybrid_preferred); the tier is standard (send_email, medium impact, contact_info, risk_score 450), so the effective mode is hybrid_preferred, which requires the classical signature.
_keys: Every signature is made with the committed TEST-ONLY keys of tests/interop/v2/interop_vectors.json#test_keys (principal and agent).
_randomness: Construction, timestamps, nonce and Ed25519 signatures are deterministic; ML-DSA-65 signatures are hedged, so regeneration is not byte-identical. The committed file is the artifact.

positives.name: session_issued_before_expires
positives.construction: re-signed: manifest (session_issued_at 5 s and session_expires_at 10 s after the verification time), manifest_hash and bundle composite signature
positives.rule: V2-4: the twin of session_issued_after_expires: not expired, issued within the 30 s skew, and issued before it expires.

cases.name: rpr_classical_sig_b64_trailing_bits
cases.construction: byte-preserving: the decoded signature bytes are unchanged, nothing re-signed
cases.rule: V2-5: every sig_b64, in the bundle signature, the artifacts’ and the checkpoints’, MUST be canonical base64 (padded, zero trailing bits).

cases.name: passport_classical_sig_b64_trailing_bits
cases.construction: byte-preserving: the decoded signature bytes are unchanged, nothing re-signed
cases.rule: V2-5: every sig_b64, in the bundle signature, the artifacts’ and the checkpoints’, MUST be canonical base64 (padded, zero trailing bits).

cases.name: policy_decision_classical_sig_b64_trailing_bits
cases.construction: byte-preserving: the decoded signature bytes are unchanged, nothing re-signed
cases.rule: V2-5: every sig_b64, in the bundle signature, the artifacts’ and the checkpoints’, MUST be canonical base64 (padded, zero trailing bits).

cases.name: checkpoint_classical_sig_b64_trailing_bits
cases.construction: byte-preserving: the decoded signature bytes are unchanged, nothing re-signed
cases.rule: V2-5: every sig_b64, in the bundle signature, the artifacts’ and the checkpoints’, MUST be canonical base64 (padded, zero trailing bits).

structural_failures: checkpoint ckpt-structural-001: classical sig_b64 not canonical

cases.name: checkpoint_without_pq
cases.construction: re-signed: checkpoint composite signature, classical component only (binding classical_only, pq null)
cases.rule: V2-12 (3): both the classical and the PQ signature MUST be present and valid (in pq_only mode, the PQ one); this holds in every mode, including the hybrid_preferred mode of this corpus, which would accept an artifact without PQ.

cases.name: checkpoint_classical_invalid_pq_resigned
cases.construction: re-signed: checkpoint classical component invalid (first byte flipped), PQ component signed again over those classical bytes
cases.rule: V2-12 (3): both the classical and the PQ signature MUST be present and valid; the effective mode here (hybrid_preferred) requires the classical one. Under pq_only, V2-12 (3) requires only the PQ one, so no pq_only verdict is claimed.

cases.name: checkpoint_range_backwards
cases.construction: re-signed: checkpoint body (from_audit_id and to_audit_id swapped) and its composite signature
cases.rule: V2-12 (2): event_range names a contiguous run of audit_entries, from the entry whose audit_id is from_audit_id to the one whose audit_id is to_audit_id, with count entries. Here from_audit_id is at trail position 2 and to_audit_id at position 1: no run goes from the first to the second. count (2) and merkle_root (over positions 1 and 2, in trail order) are what a verifier that ignored the direction would compute.

structural_failures: checkpoint ckpt-structural-001: event_range is not a forward run of the trail

cases.name: checkpoint_from_audit_id_absent
cases.construction: re-signed: checkpoint body (from_audit_id replaced by an id the trail does not hold) and its composite signature
cases.rule: V2-12 (2): the range starts at the entry whose audit_id is from_audit_id; no entry has it. count and merkle_root are those of the base range (positions 1 and 2).

structural_failures: checkpoint ckpt-structural-001: event_range names an audit_id absent from the trail

cases.name: manifest_audit_count_off_root_right
cases.construction: re-signed: manifest (audit_count 3 → 4), manifest_hash and bundle composite signature
cases.rule: V2-3: audit_count MUST equal the number of audit_entries; audit_merkle_root is the right root of the three entries. 4 exceeds the trail, so a verifier that took the first audit_count entries would still compute the right root.

cases.name: manifest_passport_hash_off
cases.construction: re-signed: manifest (passport_hash of another object), manifest_hash and bundle composite signature
cases.rule: V2-3: recompute each artifact hash from the canonical payload and verify it matches the manifest value and the artifact payload_hash; the passport payload_hash is right, the manifest value is not.

cases.name: manifest_policy_hash_off
cases.construction: re-signed: manifest (policy_hash of another object), manifest_hash and bundle composite signature
cases.rule: V2-3: as for passport_hash, with the policy decision.

cases.name: intent_payload_fraction
cases.construction: one member set after signing; nothing can be re-signed (no dcp-jcs-v1 form exists)
cases.rule: V2-3: a payload that cannot be canonicalized fails verification; dcp-jcs-v1 (spec/CANONICALIZATION_PROFILE.md) accepts integers only, so 0.5 has no canonical form. intent.target is open, so the payload stays schema-valid.

cases.name: session_issued_after_expires
cases.construction: re-signed: manifest (session_issued_at 20 s and session_expires_at 10 s after the verification time), manifest_hash and bundle composite signature
cases.rule: V2-4: reject the bundle when session_issued_at is after session_expires_at. At the corpus instant the session has not expired and session_issued_at is within the 30 s skew V2-4 allows, so only the order is wrong.

cases.name: bundle_classical_invalid_pq_resigned
cases.construction: bundle classical component invalid (first byte flipped), PQ component signed again over those classical bytes; the manifest is unchanged
cases.rule: V2-6: verify the classical signature over DCP-AI.v2.Bundle || 0x00 || canonical(manifest) with the RPR binding key; the PQ signature over those classical bytes is valid, so V2-7 does not fail. The effective mode here (hybrid_preferred) requires the classical signature; pq_only is not claimed.

isolation_limits: intent_payload_fraction: a fraction has no dcp-jcs-v1 form, so no payload_hash, manifest commitment or signature can be made over it; the base ones are kept and are stale, and any verifier rejects the bundle on them too. The case shows the verdict, not that dcp-jcs-v1 alone rejects; it is not a validly signed bundle under any normative profile, and no other profile is used to sign it.

checkpoint_range_backwards: no merkle_root can be right for a run that does not exist; the one kept is that of the same two entries in trail order, so only the direction differs from the base. A range with a gap cannot be written without a count or a merkle_root that disagrees with the named run, which bundle_vectors.json already covers (pq_checkpoint_event_range_count_wrong, pq_checkpoint_merkle_root_other).

session_issued_after_expires: with session_issued_at after session_expires_at and the session not expired, session_issued_at is necessarily after the verification time; it stays within the 30 s skew, and the twin positive (issued 5 s after that instant) is its control, so a verifier without that skew fails the control and the negative is not counted.

The sig_b64 cases use the classical component and one byte-preserving mechanism, non-zero trailing bits: an ML-DSA-65 signature (3309 bytes, a multiple of 3) has no padding and no trailing bits, so this mechanism does not apply to it. Other non-canonical forms that a permissive decoder maps to the same bytes (ignored whitespace or other characters, for instance) are not covered here; bundle_vectors.json has some for the bundle PQ sig_b64 only (a newline, extra padding, trailing junk).
